blocks.text: Why drafting detailed podcast show notes feels like a chore

The core issue is the sheer volume of manual work. You record an hour of audio, then spend another two hours transcribing, summarizing, and formatting text. This is a repetitive cycle that eats into your creative time. Many producers try to do it all at once, leading to fatigue.
Common mistakes when writing show notes

items: Trying to write everything from memory without a transcript.
Starting every set of notes from a blank page instead of using a template.
Over-editing the summary, which adds unnecessary hours to your week.
Ignoring the SEO benefits of well-structured notes.

blocks.text: Simple fixes for your writing workflow

You do not need expensive software to fix this. Start by creating a standard template in Google Docs. Include sections for a summary, key takeaways, guest bios, and links. Keep your template simple. Use it for every episode. This reduces decision fatigue.
How Lazur helps with your writing

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. When you hold the fn key, you can dictate your initial thoughts or summaries directly into your document. It helps you draft faster by turning your spoken ideas into clean text. You can also ask Lazur to summarize research notes you have open in your browser.

faq.question: Can Lazur write my entire show notes page?
faq.answer: Lazur assists by drafting text and summarizing research, but you remain the editor. It does not replace your unique voice.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen and listens to you while you hold the shortcut keys. Your content is not used to train AI models.
